newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Kidnappings unabated in Philippines, group says.
newsitem.headline: Kidnappings unabated in Philippines, group says.

text.p: Kidnap gangs have seized 42 people since January, bolstering the Philippines' image as the kidnapping centre of Asia, an anti-crime watchdog group said on Monday.

The gangs collected more than 31 million pesos ($1.2 million) in ransom from relatives of the 42 victims, who included members of prominent Filipino-Chinese families, the Movement for Restoration of Peace and Order said in a statement.

It said 242 people were kidnapped around the country in 1996 and 23 of them died -- murdered by their captors or of illness while in captivity or killed during a shootout between the kidnappers and security forces.
Ransom collected by the gangs last year totalled about 110 million pesos ($4.2 million), according to MRPO records.
"Kidnap masterminds and their protectors are getting away with impunity because in this country...crime pays and pays lucratively," MRPO chairwoman Teresita Ang See said.
See said a description of the Philippines in a recent article in the U.S. magazine Fortune as "the kidnapping capital of Asia" was accurate.
"No other Asian country has suffered more than we have (from kidnappers)," she added.

Families of kidnap victims generally refuse to cooperate with the authorities because of widespread suspicion, officially acknowledged in some cases, that police and soldiers either protect the gangs or are their masterminds.

National police chief Recaredo Sarmiento said last week calling the Philippines Asia's kidnapping capital was unfair and that official statistics show there were only 51 kidnap-for-ransom cases reported to the police last year.
He did not specify the number of victims involved in the cases.
